@graph.description: RO-Crate metadata for the AQARION Observable Quotient research package (v42 snapshot, 2026-08-04).

@graph.name: AQARION — Observable Quotient Theory for Finite Dynamical Systems
@graph.description: Research package for exact and approximate observable quotients of finite deterministic dynamical systems. Central object is the defect operator D_Π = (I − P_Π) K P_Π. Package contains definitions, computational certificates, empirical Ulam/gradient experiments, modularity analysis, quantum-DFS analogy notes, and adversarial status locks. Evidence classes are explicit: Theorem / Verified computation / Empirical / Conjecture.

@graph.name: AQARION Academy (research snapshot)
@graph.description: Internal research packaging; not a formal publisher.

@graph.name: Observable Defect Operator
@graph.description: D_Π = (I − P_Π) K P_Π, where K is the Koopman (pullback) operator and P_Π is the orthogonal projector onto functions constant on blocks of partition Π. Measures leakage of observables out of the observable subspace after one dynamical step.

@graph.name: Exactness Criterion
@graph.description: D_Π = 0 if and only if K(V_Π) ⊆ V_Π, where V_Π = Im(P_Π). Algebraic consequence of the definition when P_Π is an orthogonal projector.

@graph.name: Congruence Correspondence (Paper I centerpiece)
@graph.description: Claim: D_Π = 0 ⇔ Π ∈ Con(X,T) for a finite deterministic system (X,T). Algebraic direction is immediate; full dynamical chain (invariance → constant on blocks → well-defined quotient → congruence) requires a complete published proof.
@graph.comment: Strong but incomplete; full written proof still required.

@graph.name: Principal-Angle Identity (Frobenius form)
@graph.description: Under the hypotheses that K is unitary (or isometric on the relevant subspace) and P is an orthogonal projector onto an r-dimensional subspace V, ||(I−P)KP||_F² = Σ sin² θ_i where θ_i are the principal angles between V and K(V). Operator-norm sibling δ(V)=sin θ_max appears independently in Haseli–Cortés (arXiv:2311.13033).
@graph.comment: Standard geometry; publish with explicit hypotheses. Numeric verification at machine precision available.

@graph.name: Continuous Defect Conjecture (AQ-CONJ-CONT-001)
@graph.description: Conjecture relating Hilbert–Schmidt defect of an observable subspace to vanishing of a restricted Lyapunov spectrum. Supported by Ulam sweeps on quadratic maps (empirical correlation only). Not established as a theorem.

@graph.name: Quantum Decoherence-Free Subspace Analogy
@graph.description: Formal identity D = (I−P)UP is algebraically identical to the classical residual. Full CPTP / Kraus theory is not automatic. Status: plausible analogy, separate mathematical development required.
